grammar.title: Informal "but": 可是 and 不过
grammar.explanation: 可是 (kěshì) and 不过 (búguò) both mean "but, however" and are more conversational than 但是. 不过 is a little softer, often adding a small exception rather than a strong contrast.

grammar.title: Finishing an action with V + 完
grammar.explanation: 完 (wán) attached right after a verb shows that the action is finished "to finish doing something". It tells you the action reached its end, not just that time passed.

sentences.zh: 我很想去，可是没有时间。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, kěshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
sentences.en: I really want to go, but I don't have time.

sentences.zh: 这个电影不错，可是太长了。
sentences.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng búcuò, kěshì tài cháng le.
sentences.en: This movie is good, but it's too long.

sentences.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù, búguò méiyǒu jīhuì.
sentences.en: He wants to go, but there's no opportunity.

sentences.zh: 这个计划不错，不过太贵了。
sentences.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà búcuò, búguò tài guì le.
sentences.en: This plan is good, but it's too expensive.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ kàn wán zhè běn shū le ma?
sentences.en: Have you finished reading this book?

sentences.pinyin: Tā yī shuō wán jiù zǒu le.
sentences.en: As soon as she finished speaking, she left.
